page: Microsoft Azure E4_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is limited to a bundled 102 GB volume, and there are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the E4_v3 sits in the lower tiers for compute and memory throughput. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall within the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as large-block read and write operations, also rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the older architecture of the Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 platform. Database operations, evaluated via PassMark and Redis SET benchmarks, show weak to poor performance, with Redis achieving 2.43 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4_v3 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without the premium price of newer-generation hardware, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. The instance is suited for relational databases with moderate transaction volumes, caching layers, and enterprise applications that require a larger memory footprint but are not highly sensitive to CPU latency or memory bandwidth constraints.
